name: Core

actions.label: Set SSH Key
actions.description: Assign a Key Store key to this server (key reference is "<keyStoreNodeId>:<keyName>"). With install=true, also append the key's public half to the remote's authorized_keys using the server's current credentials.

install.description: Also install the public key on the remote's authorized_keys (default: false)

actions.label: Accept Host Key
actions.description: Scan the remote host key and pin it into known_hosts so OpenSSH-based transports (e.g. docker over ssh://) stop failing host-key verification.

actions.label: Generate Key
actions.description: Generate a new SSH keypair in this Key Store. Returns the key name and type — never private key material.

actions.label: List Keys
actions.description: List keys in this store with their type and fingerprint. Does not expose private key material.

actions.label: Delete Key
actions.description: Delete a key (and its public key) from this store.

name.description: Name of the key to delete

actions.label: Generate Secret
actions.description: Create or rotate a secret with a server-side random value. Absent name creates it, existing name rotates it. Returns the name and created/rotated status — never the value.

name.description: Secret name to create or rotate

actions.description: Execute the script in the connected terminal context (or local if none).

actions.label: Send
actions.description: Deliver a message to an agent through this node — same routing as a wired text-in delivery (session reuse/create, envelope composition, hidden-by-default registration). agent/job fall back to this node's configured defaults when omitted. Returns the target session key, whether a new session was created, and whether force actually interrupted a running turn — never the message content.

agent.description: Target agent slug; falls back to this node's default agent

job.description: Target job slug; falls back to this node's default job

key.description: Optional session discriminator — same agent+job with a different key is a distinct, stable session

title.description: Optional session title, applied only when the session is first created

session.description: Legacy combined "agent:<agent>:<job>" key, honored when agent/job are omitted

force.description: Cancel the agent's in-flight turn (if any) and enqueue this message after whatever's already queued, instead of waiting behind it. This interrupts the agent mid-work — use for urgent/corrective messages, not routine sends. No effect if the session isn't currently running a turn.

actions.label: List Agents
actions.description: Enumerate the agents (and their jobs) this node can route to via `send` — same space, same slug resolution, so any value returned here is guaranteed to route.

actions.label: List Sessions
actions.description: List the sessions this node can reach (same agent/job resolution as `send`) — compact navigation info only, never message content. Each session's `status` is the same offline/idle/working/waiting vocabulary the chat list uses: waiting = blocked on a permission request, working = a turn is running, idle = process alive but neither, offline = no process. Each also carries `contextUsage`: `{ usedTokens, contextLimit }` as last reported by that session's own harness, never estimated here. `contextUsage` is null when it is UNKNOWN — an offline session, one that has not finished a turn since it was loaded, or a harness that does not report usage — and null must not be read as "nothing held"; `contextLimit` alone is null when the harness cannot say what the model's window is, so a ratio cannot always be computed. Use it to spot a session that should be compacted before it fills (see the `compact` action). Optionally filter by agent and/or job slug.

agent.description: Only sessions for this agent slug

job.description: Only sessions for this job slug

actions.label: List Turns
actions.description: Tail-first, cursor-paged view of a session's turns (a sessionKey from listSessions) — truncated prompt/final-message text only, never the full event stream. Omit beforeIndex for the most recent turns; pass a previous page's nextBeforeIndex to page further back. Response includes `sessionStatus` (same vocabulary as listSessions): `offline` means the session has no live process, so an empty `turns` array there means "nothing to load", not "empty session". A turn's own `status` is `unknown` when it was restored by a session/load replay after a restart — it ended, but the replay does not record how, so treat it as neither success nor failure.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions

turns.description: Number of turns to return (default 10, capped at 50)

beforeIndex.description: Cursor from a previous page's nextBeforeIndex — fetches the turns immediately before it

actions.label: Compact Session
actions.description: Compact a live session's context: runs the agent's own `/compact`, then re-sends that session's task context and standing instructions, because compaction summarises the conversation and drops the original messages — including the ones that carried them. The re-send is part of this action, so a caller cannot forget it. `contextUsageBefore`/`contextUsageAfter` (same shape and same null-means-unknown rule as listSessions) BRACKET THE `/compact` TURN ALONE — the after-reading is taken before any instructions are re-sent, so it reports what compaction freed and is not reduced by the cost of restoring them. `compacted` is true when the held context shrank, false when it GREW (a harness with no `/compact` answers it as an ordinary message, so it ends up holding more — this is the failure signal, not a clean delivery), and null when it cannot be told: usage unknown on either side, or an unchanged figure, which is indistinguishable from a reading that has not refreshed. The instruction re-send is gated on that verdict — it runs on true and on null, and is SKIPPED on false, since nothing was dropped and appending instructions there would only grow the context this action exists to shrink; `instructionsRestored` reports which happened, and is also false when the session had no task context or instructions at all. Requires an IDLE session, and errors rather than half-working on any other: an `offline` session has no context to compact, and a `working` or `waiting` one has a turn in flight, which would leave `/compact` queued behind it rather than run now — so check `status` from listSessions first and compact the idle ones, retrying the others later. On an idle session the call still blocks for as long as the compaction turn itself takes (bounded; on timeout it reports usage as unknown rather than a stale figure). WHEN to compact is the caller's policy, not this action's — a typical threshold is 500k tokens held.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions
